args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money per FIN-212

The nightly build fails because tests/test_money.py expects banker's
rounding while src/money.py used ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to
ROUND_HALF_EVEN so half-cent amounts round to the nearest even cent.

args.body:
## Summary
`src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `round_money`, but per FIN-212 it must use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail (`tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`).

## Changes
- Switch rounding mode in `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on `fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212` @ 08d3cd5986: **passed**.

**Fix:** `src/money.py`'s `round_money` docstring promised banker's rounding per FIN-212, but the code used `ROUND_HALF_UP`. I switched the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` so half-cent amounts round to the nearest even cent (e.g., `2.665 → 2.66`).

**Process:**
1. Created branch `fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212` from main
2. Committed the one-line fix with an explanatory message
3. Ran CI (run `ci-0001`) — **passed**
4. Opened PR #101 against main with the code owner as reviewer
5. Merged the PR — the code owner approved it ("Looks right"), so the fix is now in main and will ship in today's release.

transcript.reasoning_content: Note: 2.675 quantized to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_EVEN — Decimal("2.675") is exact, so HALF_EVEN gives 2.68 (7 is odd → round up to even? 2.675 → half is between 2.67 and 2.68; ROUND_HALF_EVEN rounds to even last digit: 2.68 (8 even) vs 2.67 (7 odd) → 2.68. Yes. 2.665 → 2.66 (6 even) vs 2.67 → 2.66. So just change ROUND_HALF_UP to ROUND_HALF_EVEN. The docstring already says banker's rounding. Simple fix.
